root_cause: A single ARM64 CPU functional smoke test (PoolingLayerCPUTest MaxPool, ACL primitive variant) asserts the executed node's selected implementation type equals 'acl_f32', but at runtime it executed with 'undef_f32' (no implementation type recorded), i.e. the ARM Compute Library (ACL) pooling executor was not selected/attached for this MaxPool configuration in this run. Only 1 of 71707 executed smoke tests failed, and the triggering commit (#38859, 'Fold FakeQuantize output shift in ACL pooling') only touches the quantized (u8/i8) FakeQuantize destination-quantization branch of AclPoolingExecutor::init, which is not exercised by this f32, non-quantized MaxPool test case. This is consistent with the previously recorded 'smoke_AvgPool_CPU_4D ... undef_f32 vs acl_f32' pattern (signature d94563b07437b23b, first seen 2026-09-30), indicating a recurring, intermittent ACL pooling-executor selection/fallback issue that affects different pooling test instantiations (AvgPool, now MaxPool) rather than a regression from this specific commit.
reproduction_steps: Build OpenVINO for ARM64 with ACL enabled (ENABLE_ACL=ON) and run: `./ov_cpu_func_tests --gtest_filter='*smoke_MaxPool_CPU_4D/PoolingLayerCPUTest.CompareWithRefs*K_2.2_*S_2.2_*ceil*same_lower*primitive=acl*'` repeatedly; failure appears intermittent (only 1/71707 smoke tests failed in this run) and may not reproduce deterministically outside the exact ARM64 CI runner/build.
recommended_actions: Re-run the specific failing test case in isolation on the same ARM64 runner to confirm flakiness vs. a deterministic regression.

Inspect src/plugins/intel_cpu/src/nodes/executors/acl/acl_pooling.cpp::isSupported / NEPoolingLayer::validate selection path for the MaxPool K(2,2) S(2,2) PB(0,0) PE(0,0) ceil/same_lower configuration to see whether ACL silently rejects this shape/padding combination and falls back to undef instead of a different (logged) backend.
Cross-reference with pattern d94563b07437b23b (AvgPool variant) to determine whether both failures share a common root cause in executor-selection/priority logic rather than being independent flakes.

If confirmed non-reproducible/flaky, consider adding stricter DEBUG_LOG output on ACL pooling executor fallback so future occurrences are diagnosable without re-running, or add a temporary known-flaky marker referencing this signature.
prevention_strategies: Add explicit logging/telemetry in AclPoolingExecutor::isSupported when NEPoolingLayer::validate fails or ACL is skipped, so intermittent pooling-executor selection issues become deterministically traceable instead of surfacing as a single flaky smoke-test failure. Consider tracking recurring 'primType is unexpected: undef_f32' pooling failures with a dedicated CI label distinct from genuine regressions.
historical_context: A closely related failure was previously recorded: pattern d94563b07437b23b, 'smoke_AvgPool_CPU_4D fails on ACL primitive type check (undef_f32 vs acl_f32)' (first/last seen 2026-09-30, count=1, from run 36698768818, PR #38484). That investigation concluded the issue was an intermittent ACL pooling-executor selection fallback unrelated to the triggering commit. The current MaxPool failure is a distinct test instantiation but the identical primTypeCheck symptom, suggesting a shared underlying intermittent ACL pooling-executor issue worth tracking as a recurring class of flakiness.
